title: Normalization commutes with the further purely inseparable extension
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field] and let $C$ be an integral finite-type $k$-scheme [def-pc-integral-scheme, def-weil-finite-type-morphism, def-pc-scheme]. Let $k_1/k$ and $k_2/k_1$ be finite purely inseparable extensions [def-pc-field-extension, def-weil-pbc-finite-purely-inseparable-extension]. For $i=1,2$ put $C_{k_i}=C\times_{\operatorname{Spec}k}\operatorname{Spec}k_i$ [def-pc-fibre-product]; its reduction $(C_{k_i})_{\mathrm{red}}$ [def-weil-pbc-scheme-reduction] is an integral scheme, and let $\nu_i:N_i\to(C_{k_i})_{\mathrm{red}}$ be its normalization [def-sc-normalization], viewed over $C_{k_i}$. Assume that $N_1$ is geometrically normal over $k_1$: for every field extension $L/k_1$, every local ring of $N_1\times_{\operatorname{Spec}k_1}\operatorname{Spec}L$ is an integrally closed domain [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring]. Then there is a unique isomorphism $N_2\cong N_1\times_{\operatorname{Spec}k_1}\operatorname{Spec}k_2$ [def-pc-base-change] of schemes over $C_{k_2}$, where the right side maps to $C_{k_1}\times_{\operatorname{Spec}k_1}\operatorname{Spec}k_2=C_{k_2}$ by $\nu_1\times\mathrm{id}$; and $N_2$ is geometrically normal over $k_2$ in the same sense. Under this identification, for every closed subscheme $D_1\subseteq N_1$ [def-weil-closed-immersion], the reduced inverse image [def-weil-pbc-scheme-reduction] of $D_1$ in $N_2$ is $(D_1\times_{\operatorname{Spec}k_1}\operatorname{Spec}k_2)_{\mathrm{red}}$ [def-pc-fibre-product]; in particular, if $D_1$ is finite over $k_1$ [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], this reduced inverse image is finite over $k_2$.

source.place: Tags 0C3N (varieties-lemma-normalization-and-change-of-fields: canonical comparison, isomorphism for separable and universal homeomorphism in general), 038M (varieties-definition-geometrically-normal) and 038O (varieties-lemma-geometrically-normal); the geometric-normality hypothesis on N_1 makes N_1 x k_2 normal, integral and finite birational over (C_{k_2})_red, which upgrades the comparison of 0C3N to an isomorphism for the purely inseparable extension k_2/k_1.
